assertion_analysis.failure_condition: Reverting the lease (promotion.complete writing without _promotion_host_lease) makes both racing processes land, so len(landed)==1 and len(refused)==1 fail; this is the condition the negative-control.log demonstrates at base, where the cross-host case fails by id. The pid/job naming assertions at lines 309-310 are independent: the winner's pid is its own os.getpid() printed by the driver, while the refusal text is read by the loser from the lease file the winner wrote.

Removing the lease from complete lets promote_review_run_itself promote, so report["promoted"] is no longer False at line 357 and a ledger row appears at line 362; this is the second case the negative control fails by id. The holder names asserted at lines 358-360 are supplied by the test's own _held_lease call, but flow through the code's read of the lease file rather than echoing a parameter, so they are independent of the code's internals.

This case passes at both revisions (the negative control reports 1 passed at base), so it guards nothing the change introduced; it would only redden if a stale lease were refused (the _promote call raising CrewError), a behaviour the change must preserve but does not create.

findings.text: follow-on: assert promoted["run_id"] == REVIEW_RUN_ID compares the value the test itself handed to _promote (REVIEW_RUN_ID, the promotion's input) against the code's echo of it; both sides move together, so the line is true whatever the code does and would survive any regression of the lease. The test's real guard is the absence of a CrewError from _promote, which the surrounding ledger assertion at line 338 exercises; the echoed run_id adds no coverage.

follow-on: the done_when asks the cross-host case to show 'exactly one commit', but line 315 asserts only int(rev-list --count HEAD) > before (at least one). Two promotions at the base revision both commit, so this assertion does not distinguish one commit from two and cannot redden on the exact defect the done_when names; the strict count is only implied by the len(landed)==1 assertion at line 304, which does redden.
